highlights: Victoria Memorial and the Maidan
Howrah Bridge and the Hooghly riverfront
Indian Museum, one of the oldest museums in the country
College Street book market and the old coffee houses
Kumartuli, where clay idols are made before festivals
Street food such as phuchka, kathi rolls and mishti doi
kolkata.bestTime: October to February is cool and dry. Durga Puja (usually in October) is the biggest festival and the city is extremely crowded then, so book transport and hotels well ahead. Summers are hot and humid, and the monsoon (roughly June to September) brings heavy rain and waterlogging.
kolkata.gettingAround: The Kolkata Metro is fast and cheap for north-south travel. Trams still run on some routes, and yellow taxis and app-based cabs are widely available. Agree the fare or use the meter, and expect slow traffic on weekdays.
safety: Petty theft and pickpocketing occur in crowded markets, buses and the metro at peak times, so keep valuables inside your bag.
Taxi and rickshaw drivers may quote inflated prices to visitors. Use a meter or app, or agree the fare first.
Road crossings are chaotic. Watch the traffic rather than relying on signals.
Waterlogging in heavy monsoon rain can disrupt travel and airport transfers.
health: Heat and humidity can cause dehydration from April to September. Drink bottled or filtered water.
Street food is a highlight but a common cause of stomach upsets. Choose busy stalls with freshly cooked food.
Dengue risk rises during and after the monsoon, so use repellent.
tips: Carry small notes for taxis and tips.
Many museums and monuments close on one weekday, so check opening days.
Dress modestly when visiting temples, mosques and churches.

highlights: Tea estates and tea tasting
Sunrise over Kanchenjunga from Tiger Hill when the sky is clear
The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway ('toy train'), a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Batasia Loop and the Peace Pagoda
Himalayan Mountaineering Institute and the zoo
Tibetan and Nepali food and markets
darjeeling.bestTime: March to May and October to November usually offer the clearest mountain views. Winters are cold and can be foggy. The monsoon (June to September) brings heavy rain, cloud and landslides that can block roads.
darjeeling.gettingAround: Most visitors reach Darjeeling by shared or private jeep from Siliguri, New Jalpaiguri or Bagdogra (a few hours on winding mountain road). In town, many places are walkable but steep, and taxis are the practical option for sights outside the centre.
safety: Landslides on mountain roads are a real risk in the monsoon. Check road conditions before travelling.
Local strikes (bandhs) have disrupted transport in the hills in the past. Check local news and keep a flexible schedule.
Mountain roads are narrow and steep. Avoid night driving.
Weather changes quickly, so carry layers and rain protection.
health: At around 2,000 metres, altitude effects are usually mild, but take it easy on arrival.
It gets cold at night even outside winter, so pack warm clothing.
Carry any motion-sickness medicine for the winding road.
tips: Book jeeps and the toy train in advance in peak season.
Early-morning sunrise trips need an early start and warm clothing.
Cloud can hide the peaks, so allow more than one night.

highlights: Monasteries and Buddhist heritage
Orchid and flower nurseries
Viewpoints such as Durpin Dara and Deolo Hill
Hill-town markets and local crafts
Day trips towards the Teesta River and nearby villages
kalimpong.bestTime: March to May and October to November are usually clearest and mildest. The monsoon brings heavy rain and landslide risk, and winter evenings are cold.
kalimpong.gettingAround: Shared and private jeeps connect Kalimpong with Siliguri and Darjeeling. Within town, walking and local taxis cover most sights.
safety: Landslides can close roads in heavy rain, so keep your schedule flexible.
Mountain roads are narrow. Choose experienced drivers and avoid night travel.
Local strikes can affect transport, so check the news.
health: At roughly 1,200 metres, altitude is not a concern for most people.
Carry warm clothes and rain gear.
tips: Kalimpong is quieter than Darjeeling and suits a slower pace.
Many nurseries and monasteries have set visiting hours, so check before you go.

highlights: The Singalila ridge trek along the India–Nepal border
Views of Everest, Kanchenjunga, Lhotse and Makalu on clear days
Rhododendron blooms in spring
Forest villages and trekkers' huts along the route
Singalila National Park wildlife, including red pandas (rarely seen)
sandakphu.bestTime: Spring (about April to May) for rhododendrons and autumn (about October to November) for clear skies. Winter brings snow and severe cold, and the monsoon brings cloud, leeches and limited views.
sandakphu.gettingAround: The trek usually starts from Manebhanjan near Darjeeling and follows the ridge. Some visitors use jeeps along the rough track instead of walking. Accommodation is in simple trekkers' huts and lodges, so book ahead in peak season and carry cash.
safety: This is a high-altitude trek on a border ridge. Altitude sickness can affect fit people, so ascend gradually and descend if symptoms worsen.
Weather can turn quickly, with cold, wind and fog. Carry proper layers and rain protection.
The ridge runs along the border with Nepal. Keep to the marked route and carry your passport and permits.
Mobile coverage is patchy to absent. Tell someone your plan.
health: Know the symptoms of acute mountain sickness (headache, nausea, dizziness) and do not ignore them.
Facilities are basic and the nearest hospital is far away, so carry a first-aid kit and your regular medicines.
Check that your travel insurance covers trekking at altitude.
tips: Confirm current entry requirements, fees and any guide rules with the West Bengal Forest Department before you go.
Pack warm layers even in spring and autumn, and carry cash because ATMs are not available on the route.

highlights: Boat safaris through the world's largest mangrove forest
The Royal Bengal tiger's habitat (sightings are rare)
Estuarine crocodiles, spotted deer, monitor lizards and many birds
Watchtowers, creeks and riverside villages
A UNESCO World Heritage Site and tiger reserve
sundarbans.bestTime: November to February is the cooler, drier season and the most popular. Summers are hot and humid, and the monsoon brings rough water. Cyclone seasons (roughly April to May and October to November) can disrupt travel.
sundarbans.gettingAround: Visits are organised by boat from the delta region south of Kolkata, often as a one- to three-night package with an authorised operator. Timing depends on the tides, and the journey includes road transfers and boat rides.
safety: This is genuine tiger and crocodile country. Stay on the boat or on designated walkways and follow your guide strictly.
Never enter the water or go ashore except at permitted spots.
Weather and cyclone warnings can change plans, so check forecasts and keep your schedule flexible.
Use an authorised operator and permit, and be wary of unofficial offers.
health: Facilities are basic and medical help is far away, so carry a first-aid kit and your regular medicines.
Mosquitoes can be heavy. Use repellent and cover up.
Drink only sealed or filtered water.
tips: Mobile coverage is limited. Tell someone at home your itinerary.
Sightings of tigers are uncommon, so go for the landscape and wildlife as a whole.
Confirm permits and fees, which can differ for foreign visitors, with the West Bengal Forest Department or your operator.

highlights: A gateway to Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Sikkim and the Dooars
Nearby tea gardens and forests
Markets and a wide choice of hotels and transport
A practical stop to change vehicles or break a journey
siliguri.bestTime: Siliguri is a transit city, so plan around your onward destination. Winters are cool, summers hot and humid, and the monsoon is wet.
siliguri.gettingAround: Bagdogra Airport and New Jalpaiguri (NJP) railway station serve the area. Shared and private jeeps run to the hills, and local taxis and auto-rickshaws move you around the city.
safety: Touts at stations and bus stands may quote high prices. Use prepaid counters or agree fares first.
Traffic is busy. Watch your belongings in crowded areas.
If you plan onward travel to Sikkim, the hills or border areas, check permit and strike news in advance.
health: Hot, humid summers can cause dehydration. Drink bottled or filtered water.
Dengue risk rises after the monsoon, so use repellent.
tips: Book onward jeeps and hotels in advance in peak seasons.
Allow buffer time for road delays when you have a flight to catch.

highlights: Visva-Bharati University and the Uttarayan complex linked to Rabindranath Tagore
Open-air classes, art and music traditions
Craft markets with leather, batik and terracotta items
Festivals such as Poush Mela (winter) and Basanta Utsav (spring)
A UNESCO World Heritage Site (confirm details on the UNESCO website)
shantiniketan.bestTime: October to March is pleasant. Summers are very hot, and the monsoon is humid.
shantiniketan.gettingAround: Bolpur Shantiniketan station is the main railhead, and the town is compact. Cycle-rickshaws and e-rickshaws cover most distances, and many visitors explore by bicycle.
safety: This is generally a quiet town, but festival periods are very crowded. Keep belongings secure.
Agree rickshaw fares before you ride.
health: Summer heat can be intense, so avoid midday sightseeing and drink plenty of water.
tips: Some campus areas have visiting hours and rules. Respect them and ask before photographing.
The weekend craft market is a good place to buy local goods.
Book a place in advance during festivals.

highlights: Terracotta temples such as Rasmancha, Shyam Rai and Jor Bangla
Baluchari silk saris and local crafts
The Bishnupur tradition of classical music
Historic sites such as the Dalmadal cannon
A winter festival in December
bishnupur.bestTime: October to March is the most comfortable. Summers are very hot.
bishnupur.gettingAround: Bishnupur station connects to Kolkata and other towns. Within town, cycle-rickshaws and e-rickshaws are the usual way to see the temples.
safety: The town is generally calm, but watch your belongings in crowded market areas.
Agree rickshaw fares in advance.
health: Carry water and sun protection, as sights are spread out and exposed.
Facilities are basic compared with big cities.
tips: The temples are best visited in the morning or late afternoon.
Buy crafts from recognised shops and ask about the origin.

highlights: Hazarduari Palace and its museum
Katra Mosque and historic tombs and gardens
Nizamat Imambara, one of the largest imambaras in the region
Sites linked to the Nawabs of Bengal
Local silk weaving
murshidabad.bestTime: October to March is cooler. Summers are very hot and the monsoon is humid.
murshidabad.gettingAround: Berhampore and Azimganj are the usual railheads, and local auto-rickshaws and taxis connect the sites, which are spread along the Bhagirathi river.
safety: This is a less touristed area, so expect fewer English signs and facilities.
Keep belongings secure and agree transport fares in advance.
Dress modestly when visiting religious sites.
health: Summer heat can be extreme. Carry water and avoid midday sightseeing.
Medical facilities for complex needs are limited, so carry your regular medicines.
tips: Allow a full day or more to cover the main sites.
Check the opening days and times of the palace and museum before you go.

highlights: A long, wide beach on the Bay of Bengal
Sunrise and sunset walks and local seafood
Nearby quieter beaches such as Tajpur and Mandarmani
A marine aquarium and research centre
digha.bestTime: October to February is the most pleasant. Summers are hot and humid, the monsoon brings rough seas, and storms and cyclone warnings can occur.
digha.gettingAround: Digha is reached by road or rail via Contai Road and Digha stations, and local transport is by auto-rickshaw and taxi.
safety: Sea currents can be strong. Swim only where it is permitted, and follow local advice and warnings.
Beaches are very crowded on weekends and holidays, so watch your belongings.
Check weather and cyclone warnings before you go.
health: Sun and humidity can cause dehydration, so use sun protection and drink water.
Eat seafood only from clean, busy places.
tips: Book accommodation early on weekends and holidays.
Digha is mainly a domestic holiday town, so facilities are simpler than at international resorts.

highlights: Cooch Behar Palace (Victor Jubilee Palace) built in the royal era
Madan Mohan Temple and the town's historic centre
Sagar Dighi, a large lake
Local culture and crafts of North Bengal
cooch-behar.bestTime: October to March is cool and dry. Summers are hot and humid, and the monsoon brings heavy rain.
cooch-behar.gettingAround: Cooch Behar and New Cooch Behar stations link to the rest of North Bengal. Within town, rickshaws and autos cover the main sights.
safety: The district is close to the Bangladesh border. Carry your passport and do not approach border areas without authorisation.
Keep valuables secure and agree transport fares in advance.
Facilities for foreign visitors are limited, so plan ahead.
health: Carry water and sun protection in summer.
Medical facilities for specialist care are limited.
tips: Check the opening days of the palace museum before you go.
Combine Cooch Behar with the Dooars forests for a longer North Bengal trip.

highlights: Wildlife reserves such as Jaldapara and Gorumara, known for one-horned rhinos and elephants
Jeep safaris through forest and grassland
Tea estates and forest lodges
Bird watching and river scenery
dooars.bestTime: November to March is the best season for wildlife. National parks are generally closed or limited during the monsoon, so check the dates before booking.
dooars.gettingAround: Bagdogra Airport and New Jalpaiguri (NJP) are the main gateways, with onward transport by road to the parks. Safaris are usually by jeep and need advance booking in season.
safety: Wild elephants and rhinos are dangerous. Stay inside the vehicle and follow your guide.
Do not walk in forest areas at night.
Roads can flood in heavy monsoon rain.
health: Mosquitoes can be heavy in the evenings. Use repellent.
Medical facilities in rural areas are limited, so carry a first-aid kit.
tips: Confirm park timings, closed days and entry rules with the West Bengal Forest Department.
Book forest lodges and safaris well ahead in winter.

highlights: Red Fort and Jama Masjid in Old Delhi
Humayun's Tomb and Qutub Minar, both UNESCO World Heritage Sites
India Gate and the government quarter of New Delhi
Chandni Chowk's food and bazaars
Lotus Temple, museums and craft markets
delhi.bestTime: October to March is the most comfortable, although winter air pollution and fog can be severe from about November to January. Summers (April to June) are extremely hot, and the monsoon is humid.
delhi.gettingAround: The Delhi Metro is clean, fast and the easiest way to cross the city, and an Airport Express line connects the airport to the centre. Use app-based cabs or prepaid taxis, and avoid unofficial drivers who approach you at the airport.
safety: Tourist scams are common: touts claiming a site is closed, offering a 'tourist office', or steering you to shops. Book through official counters and apps.
Pickpocketing occurs in crowded markets and the metro.
Solo women travellers should take extra care at night and use trusted transport.
Air quality can be very poor in winter. Check the air-quality index and consider a mask.
health: Heat can be dangerous in summer, so drink water and limit midday outings.
'Delhi belly' is common. Choose busy, clean places and bottled water.
Poor air quality can aggravate asthma and other conditions.
tips: Many monuments close on one day of the week, so check opening days.
Allow extra time for traffic and security checks.
Dress modestly at religious sites.

highlights: The Taj Mahal (a UNESCO World Heritage Site) at sunrise or sunset
Agra Fort
Fatehpur Sikri nearby
Mehtab Bagh for views of the Taj across the river
Mughal-era food, marble inlay and leather goods
agra.bestTime: October to March is the most comfortable. Winter fog can delay trains and flights, and summers are extremely hot. The Taj Mahal is normally closed on Fridays and can close for other reasons, so check before you go.
agra.gettingAround: Most visitors come from Delhi by train, road or the expressway, and many do it as a day trip, although staying overnight avoids the rush. In Agra, use app cabs, auto-rickshaws or electric vehicles near the Taj, since normal traffic is restricted close to it.
safety: Touts, aggressive guides and shop commissions are common. Book guides and tickets through official channels.
Agree prices in advance for rickshaws and tours.
Crowds are heavy at the Taj Mahal. Keep valuables close.
health: Heat is intense in summer. Carry water and sun protection.
Choose clean restaurants and bottled water.
tips: Buy tickets online or at official counters, and follow the security rules on what you may bring in.
Arrive early for lower crowds and softer light.

highlights: Amber Fort and the City Palace
Hawa Mahal and the Jantar Mantar observatory (UNESCO)
Nahargarh and Jaigarh forts with city views
Bazaars for textiles, jewellery and blue pottery
Rajasthani food and cultural shows
jaipur.bestTime: October to March is cool and dry. Summers are extremely hot, and the monsoon (July to September) is warm and humid. The Jaipur Literature Festival is usually held in January.
jaipur.gettingAround: App cabs, auto-rickshaws and tuk-tuks are widely available, and the metro covers parts of the city. Agree fares before you ride if there is no meter.
safety: Gem, carpet and textile shop scams are common. Do not buy high-value items on the advice of a driver or guide who earns commission.
Agree prices in advance for tours and rickshaws.
Watch your belongings in crowded markets.
health: Heat is a real hazard in summer. Drink water and limit midday outings.
Choose busy restaurants with fresh food.
tips: Visit forts early to avoid heat and crowds.
Many monuments sell combined tickets, so check what is included.
Bargain politely in markets.

highlights: Beaches in North and South Goa
Old Goa's churches and convents (UNESCO)
Fontainhas, the old Latin Quarter of Panaji
Spice plantations, forts and river cruises
Seafood, nightlife and markets
goa.bestTime: November to February is the peak season, with dry, pleasant weather. The monsoon (June to September) brings heavy rain and rough seas, when many beach shacks close and swimming can be dangerous.
goa.gettingAround: Scooter and car rentals are popular, and app cabs, local taxis and buses also run. Roads can be congested and unevenly lit, and scooter accidents involving visitors are a known problem.
safety: Sea currents can be dangerous. Swim only where lifeguards are present and follow flags and warnings.
Do not drink and drive. Road accidents are a leading risk, so wear a helmet and have a valid licence.
Drug laws are strictly enforced, and foreigners are not exempt.
Isolated beaches at night carry higher risk, particularly for women travelling alone.
Keep valuables out of sight on beaches and in rented scooters.
health: Sun and humidity can cause dehydration and sunburn.
Eat seafood only from clean, busy places.
Mosquito-borne illness increases in and after the monsoon.
tips: Prices rise sharply around Christmas and New Year, so book early.
Check which of the two airports your flight uses.
Dress modestly when visiting churches and temples.

highlights: Fort Kochi's old streets, Chinese fishing nets and colonial buildings
Mattancherry and Jew Town, with antique shops and a historic synagogue
Kathakali and other performances
Backwater trips and houseboats at nearby Alappuzha
Kerala cuisine and spice markets
kochi.bestTime: October to March is cooler and drier. The south-west monsoon (June to September) brings heavy rain, and flooding has affected the region in the past. Summers are hot and humid.
kochi.gettingAround: Ferries and the Kochi Water Metro link the waterfront areas, and app cabs, autos and buses cover the rest. Kochi also has a metro line.
safety: Kochi is generally considered easy for visitors, but watch your belongings in crowds.
Agree auto-rickshaw fares or use the meter.
Check weather warnings in the monsoon, when roads and ferries can be disrupted.
health: Humidity is high, so drink plenty of water.
Mosquito-borne illness increases around the monsoon, so use repellent.
Choose clean restaurants for seafood.
tips: For backwater cruises, compare operators and confirm what is included.
Book Kathakali shows in advance in peak season.

highlights: Shanti Stupa and Leh Palace
Monasteries such as Thiksey, Hemis and Spituk
High mountain passes and the Indus Valley
Pangong Lake and Nubra Valley (permits needed)
Treks, road trips and Ladakhi food
leh.bestTime: Roughly May or June to September is the main season, when roads are open and temperatures are mild. Winters are extremely cold, and many roads and services close, with travel mostly by air.
leh.gettingAround: Taxis are the main way to see the area and are usually organised through taxi unions at fixed rates. Overland routes from Manali and Srinagar are open only part of the year and involve high passes.
safety: Altitude sickness is the main risk. Leh is at around 3,500 metres. Rest and drink water for the first day or two, and avoid alcohol and heavy exertion until you adjust.
Do not go straight to higher places such as high passes or Pangong on arrival.
Road travel involves long, remote stretches and landslide risk. Plan for delays.
Check permit rules for restricted areas, and carry copies of your documents.
Mobile coverage is limited, and many prepaid SIM cards from outside the region do not work. Ask about postpaid or local options.
health: Know the symptoms of acute mountain sickness (headache, nausea, dizziness, breathlessness) and descend if they worsen.
Ask your doctor about altitude medication before you travel.
The sun is very strong at altitude, so use sunscreen and sunglasses.
Medical facilities are limited for serious cases, so confirm that your insurance covers evacuation.
tips: Allow at least two days to acclimatise before any high-altitude excursion.
Carry cash because ATMs and card acceptance can be unreliable.
Respect monasteries, remove shoes where required and ask before photographing people.

highlights: Yoga and meditation ashrams and classes
The evening Ganga aarti at the river ghats
Laxman Jhula and Ram Jhula suspension bridges
White-water rafting and other adventure activities (seasonal)
Cafes, bookshops and riverside walks
rishikesh.bestTime: September to November and February to April are the most pleasant. Rafting is typically closed during the monsoon (about July to September) for safety. Summers are hot, and winters are cool.
rishikesh.gettingAround: The town is spread along the Ganges. Walking, e-rickshaws and shared autos cover the main areas, and the nearest airport is at Dehradun. Haridwar station is also commonly used.
safety: Choose licensed adventure operators with certified guides and safety gear. Check that your insurance covers rafting and bungee.
River currents are strong. Bathe only in designated areas.
Monkeys can snatch food and belongings. Keep items out of sight.
Roads in the hills can be affected by landslides in the monsoon.
health: The Ganga is a sacred and busy river. Drink only sealed or properly filtered water.
Choose clean eating places.
Dress warmly at night in winter.
tips: The main riverside area is largely vegetarian and alcohol-free, in keeping with its religious character.
Dress modestly and respect ashram rules.
Check yoga schools for qualifications and book retreats in advance.

highlights: The Ridge, Mall Road and Christ Church
The Kalka–Shimla railway, a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Jakhu Temple and mountain views
Day trips to Kufri and nearby hill areas
Colonial-era architecture and cafes
shimla.bestTime: March to June and October to November are pleasant. Winters (December to February) can bring snow and sub-zero temperatures, and the monsoon (July to September) brings landslides and road disruptions.
shimla.gettingAround: Most visitors arrive by road from Chandigarh or by the narrow-gauge railway from Kalka. The town is hilly and steep, and parts of the centre are pedestrian-only, so use taxis for longer distances.
safety: Monkeys around Jakhu Temple and other areas can be aggressive. Keep food and belongings out of sight.
Mountain roads are narrow, and landslides occur in the monsoon.
In winter, snow and ice can close roads, so check conditions before you travel.
health: The altitude (around 2,200 metres) is mild, but steep walks can be tiring.
Carry warm layers, as temperatures drop quickly.
Check weather and road conditions in monsoon and winter.
tips: Book accommodation early for peak summer and for snow season.
If you plan to visit border areas such as Kinnaur or Spiti, check permit rules in advance.

highlights: City Palace complex on the shore of Lake Pichola
Boat rides on Lake Pichola at sunset
Jag Mandir and the Lake Palace seen from the water
Saheliyon-ki-Bari gardens and Jagdish Temple
Sajjangarh (Monsoon Palace) for views over the city
Old-town lanes, miniature-painting studios and puppet shows
udaipur.bestTime: October to March is cool and pleasant. Summers are very hot. The monsoon (July to September) fills the lakes and turns the hills green, but brings humid, rainy weather.
udaipur.gettingAround: The old town is walkable, though lanes are narrow and busy. Auto-rickshaws, app cabs and rented scooters cover the rest. Boats operate on the lakes, and some island palaces are reached only by boat.
safety: Commission shops are common: drivers and guides may steer you to shops or galleries. Compare prices and do not feel pressured to buy.
Scooter hire is popular but traffic is dense and roads are uneven. Wear a helmet and carry a valid licence.
Lake boats can be crowded in the evening. Wear the life jacket provided.
Agree auto-rickshaw fares in advance or use an app.
health: Summer heat is intense. Carry water and avoid midday sightseeing.
Choose clean, busy restaurants, especially for rooftop dining and street food.
Mosquito numbers rise near the lakes after the monsoon, so use repellent.
tips: Palace and museum timings vary and some days are closed, so check before you go.
Sunset boat rides and rooftop views are popular, so book ahead in peak season.
Dress modestly at temples and in the old town.

highlights: Mehrangarh Fort, one of India's largest forts, with a museum and audio tour
Jaswant Thada and the Umaid Bhawan Palace area
The blue-painted old town below the fort
Clock Tower and Sardar Market for spices, textiles and handicrafts
Mandore Gardens and desert excursions
Local food such as mirchi vada and makhaniya lassi
jodhpur.bestTime: October to March is the most comfortable. Summers are extremely hot. The monsoon is short and the city is dry for most of the year.
jodhpur.gettingAround: The old city is walkable but hilly and crowded. Auto-rickshaws and app cabs link the fort, the markets and the palace area, and many visitors hire a car for desert and village trips.
safety: Touts and commission-based shops operate near the fort and the market. Be wary of high-value purchases (gems, rugs, antiques) on a guide's advice.
Narrow lanes and traffic make the old town chaotic, so watch your belongings.
Heat is the main physical risk in summer.
Agree prices for auto-rickshaws and desert excursions before you start.
health: Carry water and sun protection. The fort involves a lot of walking and some steep ramps, though a lift is available.
Avoid street food that has been sitting out.
Desert dust can irritate people with asthma or allergies.
tips: Visit the fort early in the day to beat heat and crowds.
Respect private homes in the blue old town and ask before photographing residents.
Check opening hours of the palace and museum before you go.

highlights: Tea plantations and the tea museum
Eravikulam National Park, home to the Nilgiri tahr
Mattupetty Dam, Echo Point and Top Station viewpoints
Spice plantations and cool misty valleys
Walks and treks in the Western Ghats
The neelakurinji flower, which blooms only about once every twelve years
munnar.bestTime: September to May is generally pleasant, with cool temperatures. The south-west monsoon (June to August) brings heavy rain, mist and landslide risk. Nights can be cold, particularly from December to February.
munnar.gettingAround: Munnar is reached by long, winding mountain roads from Kochi and other towns. Local taxis and jeeps are the usual way to see viewpoints and plantations, and many visitors hire a driver for the trip.
safety: Heavy rain can cause landslides and road closures, so check conditions before you travel in the monsoon.
Mountain roads are narrow and winding. Avoid night driving.
Wild elephants can wander near plantations and roads, particularly at night. Follow local advice and do not approach wildlife.
Dense mist can reduce visibility on roads and viewpoints.
health: The air is cool, so carry warm clothing and rain protection.
Motion sickness is common on the winding approach, so carry remedies if you are prone.
Use repellent against leeches and mosquitoes in the wet season.
tips: National park entry may be restricted or closed in certain seasons. Check current rules and timings before you go.
Carry cash, as some places in hill areas may not accept cards.
Allow more than one night to enjoy the area rather than rushing.

highlights: Backwater cruises on canals and Vembanad Lake
Houseboat stays on traditional kettuvallam boats
Village life in the Kuttanad rice-growing region
Alappuzha Beach and nearby Marari Beach
Coir-making and local craft demonstrations
The Nehru Trophy Boat Race, usually held in August
alappuzha.bestTime: November to February is the most comfortable and the main season. Summers are hot and humid, and the monsoon brings heavy rain and rougher water.
alappuzha.gettingAround: The town is linked by road and rail to Kochi and other Kerala towns. Boats, ferries and houseboats are the main way to see the backwaters, and local ferries are an inexpensive alternative to private cruises.
safety: Choose a houseboat from a registered operator and check life jackets, fire safety and what is included before you book.
Weather and water conditions can change quickly in the monsoon, so confirm trips are running.
Avoid swimming in the backwaters unless a guide says it is safe.
Agree prices for boats, autos and tours in advance.
health: Humidity is high, so drink plenty of bottled or filtered water.
Use mosquito repellent, particularly in the evening.
Choose clean restaurants for seafood and make sure food is cooked well.
tips: Compare private and shared cruises and check whether meals and overnight stays are included.
Book houseboats early during the peak winter season.
Respect village life and ask before photographing people.

highlights: Old Manali's cafes and lanes
Hadimba Temple in a cedar forest
Solang Valley for skiing, paragliding and zorbing (seasonal)
The Beas River for rafting and riverside walks
Atal Tunnel and the route towards Lahaul
Rohtang Pass area (seasonal, with vehicle rules)
manali.bestTime: March to June and September to November are pleasant for sightseeing. December to February is cold with snow at higher elevations. The monsoon (July to August) brings heavy rain, landslides and road closures.
manali.gettingAround: Taxis and local cabs are the main way to reach viewpoints and valleys, and taxi unions often set fixed rates. Getting to Manali involves a long road journey, so allow plenty of time.
safety: Monsoon rains can trigger landslides and flash floods and close roads, so check conditions before you travel and keep your schedule flexible.
Use licensed adventure operators with certified guides for paragliding, rafting and skiing, and check that your insurance covers them.
Mountain roads are narrow and winding. Avoid night driving.
Weather can change quickly at higher altitudes, so carry warm layers.
health: Altitude effects can occur at higher passes. Ascend gradually and rest if you feel unwell.
The sun is strong at altitude, so use sunscreen and sunglasses.
Carry medicines for motion sickness on the winding approach.
tips: Some high routes and passes are open only seasonally, so confirm before planning onward travel.
Book accommodation in advance for summer and the winter holidays.
Respect local rules on drugs. Possession carries severe penalties even though it is sometimes easy to find in tourist areas.

highlights: McLeod Ganj and the Tsuglagkhang complex, the Dalai Lama's temple
Tibetan monasteries, museums and cafes
Bhagsu Waterfall and the nearby village
The Triund trek with views of the Dhauladhar range
Tibetan handicrafts and food, including momos and thukpa
Norbulingka Institute near Sidhpur, focused on Tibetan arts
dharamshala.bestTime: March to June and September to November are generally pleasant. Winters are cold with snow in the higher areas. The monsoon (July to September) is very wet, with landslides and poor visibility.
dharamshala.gettingAround: Dharamshala is the lower town and McLeod Ganj is the upper one, linked by steep roads. Taxis and shared cabs connect them, and McLeod Ganj itself is easy to explore on foot.
safety: Heavy monsoon rain can cause landslides and flash floods. Check conditions before you travel.
Trekking to places such as Triund involves weather and terrain risks, so check the forecast, carry layers and consider a guide.
Roads are steep and winding. Avoid night driving.
Be respectful around the Tibetan community and avoid taking sides in political discussions in public.
health: Carry warm clothing, as evenings can be cold even outside winter.
Take it easy on arrival if you are not used to hill roads and climbing.
Choose clean restaurants and drink bottled or filtered water.
tips: Dress modestly and follow monastery rules on photography and behaviour.
Public talks and teachings are sometimes open to visitors. Check notices for current arrangements.
Book accommodation early in the main season.
